messages.content: You are helping a fraud-awareness instructor build quiz cards. Each card shows one text message exactly as it would appear on the recipient's phone, and students must decide whether it is safe. Cards are only useful if they are indistinguishable from the real thing, so never hint at the answer. All content is fictional. Never use a real person's name, address or account number. Any phone number in the text must be in the fictional 555-01XX range (for example 214-555-0143). Any link must use a made-up domain, except legitimate messages may use the brand's real main domain. Don't use placeholders like [Name] or <link>: write concrete fictional values instead.

Quiz topic: Wrong-number or family impersonation. The correct answer for these cards is: scam.
Background: Starts a personal conversation to build trust: a fake wrong-number text, a relative or friend writing from a 'new number' who needs money, or a romance opener.
Scenario for these cards: friendly wrong-number opener, sent as no brand.
The person receiving the text: a parent who shops online often.
Tone of the text: warm and reassuring.
Draft 8 cards, each a different realistic text. Each message should contain the kind of lure this category uses (a link, a callback number, a reply request, or a request for money or a code).
Return only JSON: {"messages": ["<text 1>", "<text 2>", ...]} with exactly 8 strings. Each string is the SMS body only, without the sender.

response: {"messages":["Hi! I think I have the wrong number – my friend gave me this as Sarah's. But since I have you, could you do me a quick favor and reply with your first name so I can update my contacts? Thanks so much!","Hey there, sorry to bother you. I was trying to reach my cousin Mike but must have typed his old number. You seem friendly – if you're not Mike, no worries. Just reply 'not Mike' and I'll delete this. Have a great day!","Hello! I'm looking for a nice family to help me test a new online shopping app – I'll send you a $50 gift card if you click this link and create a free account: shop-rewards.example.com. Totally safe, just want honest feedback. Thanks!","Hi, wrong number I think – but you sound like someone who'd be great at this: my aunt needs help with a delivery that got held up. Can you call me back at 214-555-0187 and I'll explain? She's elderly and I'm worried. Thanks!","Oops, wrong number! But since I have you – I'm trying to surprise my mom with a shopping spree. Could you reply with a quick 'yes' if you'd be willing to receive a package for her? I'll explain. You seem trustworthy.","Hey, is this Karen? No? Sorry! But you might be able to help – I'm stuck overseas and my wallet was stolen. Could you send me a small Western Union transfer? I'll pay you back double. Just reply and I'll give details. God bless.","Hi there! Wrong number, but I wanted to say you have a kind vibe. I'm new in town and trying to make friends. Want to chat? Just reply 'hi' and I'll send you my photo. Nothing weird, just lonely.","Hello! Sorry to text randomly – I meant to message my sister but got your number. She's supposed to send me a verification code for a purchase.
